---
title: "Assessment review: anchors, bias and model choice"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
params:
  run_bias: true
  run_anchors: false
  run_comparison: false
  output_dir: "assessment-review-files"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(mfrmr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 5)
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
context <- c(
  question = "Review a specified rater-criterion interaction; add linking or model sensitivity only when relevant",
  rating_unit = "One synthetic Person by Rater by Criterion rating",
  score_direction = "Illustrative interpretation: higher coded scores are more favorable",
  rubric = "Permitted scores 1 to 4; replace with the actual endpoint wording",
  transformation = "None"
)
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  method = "MML", model = "RSM", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,
  category_policy = "preserve")
diagnostics <- diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "none")
results <- mfrm_results(fit, diagnostics = diagnostics, include = "standard")
reports <- list(measurement = mfrm_report(results, style = "apa", study_context = context))
objects <- list(fit = fit, diagnostics = diagnostics, results = results)
out <- params$output_dir
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Question, units and score meaning

This is an executable **synthetic teaching example**, not a study of actual
raters or evidence that any particular rater is unfair. Choose the sections
with `run_bias`, `run_anchors` and `run_comparison`; optional analyses are not
requirements for every manuscript. For your own study, replace the data and
context, specify the sampling/assignment and exclusions, and explain why the
selected model and contrasts answer the question.

```{r context}
knitr::kable(reports$measurement$study_context)
knitr::kable(reports$measurement$first_screen[, c("Area", "Status", "MainIssue")])
```

If higher Comprehensibility values mean **harder** to understand, state that
direction explicitly. Changing this declaration does not reverse the scores
or estimated parameters. Recoding requires compatible endpoints, anchors,
model refitting and dependent output. MFRM latent estimates and raw G-study
score components are different quantities even when their labels match.

## A prespecified bias question

```{r bias, eval=params$run_bias}
bias <- estimate_bias(fit, diagnostics, facet_a = "Rater", facet_b = "Criterion")
reports$bias <- mfrm_report(bias, style = "apa", study_context = context)
objects$bias <- bias
knitr::kable(reports$bias$tables$overview, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(reports$bias$tables$bias_cells[, c("FacetA_Level", "FacetB_Level", "Bias Size",
  "S.E.", "t", "Prob.", "BiasStatus", "ScreenStatus")], digits = 3)
bias_plot <- plot(bias_interaction_report(bias), type = "scatter")
```

Report the signed contrast, cell counts and unavailable screens alongside the
screening rule. Positive Bias Size raises expected **coded** scores; it is not
automatically favorable performance. These are conditional plug-in screens.
The overview's Bonferroni/Holm counts use this interaction's whole cell family,
including unavailable cells in its size; they do not establish formal error
control or cover a search across multiple interactions. Do not select only
flagged cells for the appendix. Explain the proposed substantive follow-up;
a flag is not evidence of unfairness or a reason to exclude a rater.

For an exploratory search across facet pairs, replace the bias module's
calculation with `bias <- estimate_all_bias(fit, diagnostics)` and keep
`reports$bias <- mfrm_report(bias, study_context = context)`. Its `overview`
lists every requested interaction; `bias_cells` adds an `Interaction` key and
`errors` retains failed pairs. Use `plot(bias)` for the collection overview.
Report the search scope and full cells without claiming collection-wide error
control. A joint model chosen from these screens remains exploratory when
compared on the same data; consult the Linking and DFF guide for that route.

## Reusing anchors in a receiving cohort

```{r anchors, eval=params$run_anchors}
people <- unique(ratings$Person)
reference_data <- ratings[ratings$Person %in% people[1:24], ]
receiving_data <- ratings[ratings$Person %in% people[25:48], ]
reference_fit <- fit_mfrm(reference_data, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  method = "MML", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve")
anchors <- make_anchor_table(reference_fit, facets = "Criterion")
review <- review_mfrm_anchors(receiving_data, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  anchors = anchors, rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve")
anchor_context <- c(context, anchor_source = "Criterion locations estimated from the first 24 synthetic Persons",
  anchor_uncertainty = "Receiving fit conditions on these supplied values; source uncertainty is not propagated")
reports$anchors <- mfrm_report(review, study_context = anchor_context)
knitr::kable(reports$anchors$tables$anchors, digits = 4)
knitr::kable(reports$anchors$tables$issue_counts)
receiving_fit <- fit_mfrm(receiving_data, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  method = "MML", anchors = anchors, rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,
  category_policy = "preserve")
linking <- build_linking_review(anchor_review = review)
reports$linking <- mfrm_report(linking, study_context = anchor_context)
knitr::kable(reports$linking$tables$status)
objects$anchor_analysis <- list(reference_fit = reference_fit, receiving_fit = receiving_fit,
  anchors = anchors, review = review, linking = linking)
```

Keep full-precision internal-logit anchor values, matching identities and
score coding. State the centering and population assumptions and why the
criteria are expected to be invariant. These illustrative cohorts are disjoint,
but using their shared criterion labels does not prove invariance. This module
does not estimate drift or propagate reference-calibration uncertainty; missing
drift evidence stays missing. It does not demonstrate equivalent populations
or change a conditional SE into an unconditional one.

## Does the model choice change the answer?

```{r comparison, eval=params$run_comparison}
pcm <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score", method = "MML",
  model = "PCM", step_facet = "Criterion", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,
  category_policy = "preserve")
choice <- build_model_choice_review(RSM = fit, PCM = pcm)
reports$model_choice <- mfrm_report(choice, style = "apa", study_context = context)
knitr::kable(reports$model_choice$tables$comparison_table, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(reports$model_choice$tables$model_roles)
objects$model_choice <- list(pcm = pcm, review = choice)
```

The RSM uses a shared category-step structure; this PCM lets it vary by
criterion. Read comparability and numerical readiness before interpreting ICs.
The review does not request an LRT. If a prespecified nested-model test is
needed, call `compare_mfrm(fit, pcm, nested = TRUE)` and retain its separate
eligibility and reasons. Models must use compatible observations, weights,
estimator, identification and numerical rules. Report whether the substantive
answer or score interpretation changes, not only the smallest AIC.

## Answer and save the evidence

**Complete for your study:** answer the question, report effect magnitude and
its uncertainty or screening status, then explain limitations and the justified
action. Use `gtheory-report.Rmd` for future rating plans and `gpcm-report.Rmd`
for the one-family slope workflow. State any change in units, aggregation or
score meaning when joining those analyses; shared context is not proof of
cross-analysis equivalence.

```{r save, include=FALSE}
for (nm in names(reports)) {
  export_summary_appendix(reports[[nm]], output_dir = out, prefix = nm, overwrite = TRUE)
  writeLines(reports[[nm]]$markdown, file.path(out, paste0(nm, ".md")))
}
saveRDS(list(objects = objects, reports = reports, study_context = context,
  session = sessionInfo()), file.path(out, "assessment-review.rds"))
```

The archive retains analysis-level source information; review its contents
before sharing. Record the package archive/version and the analysis decisions
with the manuscript. For method references and additional qualifications, see
`help("estimate_bias")`, `help("review_mfrm_anchors")`, `help("compare_mfrm")`
and the installed linking and reporting tutorials.
